Tone remains broadly positive but measured: the statement emphasizes strong real activity, low unemployment, and inflation near the symmetric 2% objective with balanced risks and guidance for gradual rate hikes. Incorporating the April 2018 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, banks reported unchanged standards for qualified-mortgage jumbo residential loans, policy changes in commercial real estate (indicative of some tightening), wider loan rate spreads, and shifts in CRE loan demand, with loan demand discussed across both businesses and households. These SLOOS signals point to credit conditions that are not broadly easing—and in some segments modestly tighter—which tempers the otherwise upbeat cyclical backdrop. Netting the SLOOS evidence against the strong macro tone moves the assessment to positive-but-cautious, slightly below the prior read that leaned on the FSR alone.
